full_judgment:
AK Badrul Huq J: By this application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the petitioners challenge the correctness of a decision recorded by the learned Subordinate Judge in refusing to vacate an order staying a Small Causes Court Execution Case whereupon Rule was issued calling upon the Opposite Party No-1 to show cause as to why the order dated August 31, 1997 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Camilla in Title Suit No 27 of 1997 should not be set aside. 

 2. The portrayal of the essential facts forming the background of the issuance of the Rule is that’s the petitioners of this Rule Sree Sree Gouranga Bishnupriya represented by its Shebait, as plaintiffs laid a suit being Small Causes Court Suit No 3 of 1993 before the Small Causes Court Judge who is also the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Comilla for a decree of ejectment of the tenants on the property described in schedule to the plaint taking stand that the defendant-tenants were defaulters in payment of rent. The defendant-tenants did not contest the suit in spite of the service of notice upon them. The suit was dismissed ex parte against the defendant tenants. Plaintiffs of the said suit (petitioners) put the decree into execution in Small Causes Court Execution Case No-I of 1997. 

 3. The opposite party No 1 of this Rule, thereafter, as plaintiff instituted a suit being Title Suit No-27 of 1997 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Comilla for a declaration that the decree dated 24-8-96 recorded in Small Causes Court Suit No-3 of 1993 of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla is void and not binding upon the plaintiff. The suit is based upon an oral contract allegedly entered between the plaintiff of the present suit (opposite party No-1) and Shebaits, the defendant No 1 and 2 (petitioner No 1 and 2) for selling the suit property on a consideration of Taka 1, 50,000. Thereafter, on 1-6-1997 the plaintiff of the present suit (opposite party No 1) presented an application under the provisions of Order 21 rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceeding of SCC Execution Case No. 1 of 1997.The learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 8-6-1997 stayed the proceeding of the SCC Execution Case till disposal of the suit. The Decree Holders who are defendant Nos. 1 to 10 of this suit (petitioners), thereafter, filed a written objection against the application filed by the plaintiff (opposite party No-1) for staying the Decree Execution Case. The learned Subordinate Judge by the order dated 29-7-1997 rejected the said application recording the view that there was no scope for filing written objection against the order dated 8-6-1997. 

 (iii) The plaintiff of the suit got no locus standi to file an application for staying the proceeding of the Execution Case No. 1 of 1997. 

 (a) The order staying the proceeding of the Execution Case having been rested upon a total misconception and misapprehension of law and fact. the said order can be easily vacated by invoking the Court's inherent power under section 151 of the Code and the learned Subordinate Judge committed a substantial error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in not vacating the order staying the execution proceeding. 

 13. Admittedly, the plaintiff of the present suit (opposite party No 1) was not a party to the suit laid by the defendant Nos. 1-10 (petitioners) and the present plaintiff (opposite party No 1) was not a judgment-debtor. The plaintiff (opposite party No 1) was not at all lawfully authorised to bring any application for stay of the execution of a decree passed in previous suit ie. Title Suit No 3 of 1993 and the application under Order 21, rule 29 of the Code was absolutely misconceived and not tenable in law. The learned Subordinate Judge under a total misconception and misapprehension of law stayed the proceeding of the execution case. The plaintiff (opposite party No. 1) being a stranger or a third party to the previous decree, got no legal character nor locus standi to maintain any application for stay of the Execution proceeding of the previous suit. The order recorded by the learned Subordinate Judge in staying the Execution proceeding of the Execution case suffers from a patent illegality, legal infirmity and substantial error of law. 

 14. It had already been pointed out that the order recorded by the learned Subordinate Judge in staying the execution proceeding is not sanctioned by any law and the same has been based upon a misapprehension of law. The said order having suffered from patent error of law rendering a miscarriage of justice to the petitioners is liable to be vacated to secure the ends of justice as because courts solemn duty is to secure ends of justice and not to bury justice. 

 In the result the Rule is made absolute, however, without any order as to cost. The impugned order dated 8-6-1997 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge staying the proceeding of Small Causes Court Decree Execution Case No 1 of 1997 and the subsequent order dated 31-8-1997 refusing to vacate the said order of stay dated 8-6-1997 stand set aside. The application of the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 for staying the proceeding of SCC Execution Case No 1 of 1997 stands rejected.
